extracted.intended_audience: stabilization agencies; Office of Stabilization Administrator; Office of Price Administration; employers and legal/HR advisors seeking wage/salary adjustments under the 1945 national wage-price policy
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory provisions and standards governing pre-approval, automatic approval classes, and treatment of wage/salary adjustments under the National Wage‑Price Policy (Executive Orders of Aug. 18 and Oct. 30, 1945). Intended to guide stabilization agencies, employers, and price authorities in administering and evaluating wage/salary increase requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope / legal authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive regulations for the guidance of the stabilization agencies in administering the national wage-price policy established in the Executive Orders of August 18 and October 30, 1945.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations issued by the Office of Stabilization Administrator set the framework and procedural rules that stabilization agencies must follow when handling wage or salary adjustment requests under the cited executive orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-approval by the Stabilization Administrator
rubrics_metrics.description: PRE-APPROVAL IS GRANTED BY THE STABILIZATION ADMINISTRATOR TO WAGE OR SALARY ADJUSTMENTS WHICH ARE FOUND BY THE APPROPRIATE STABILIZATION AGENCY TO FALL WITHIN SPECIFIED CLASSES OF CASES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An adjustment must be found by the appropriate stabilization agency to fall within specified classes listed in the regulations for the Administrator to grant pre-approval. Pre-approval authority resides with the Stabilization Administrator; agencies determine whether a case falls in the specified classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic approval for specified classes
rubrics_metrics.description: WAGE OR SALARY ADJUSTMENTS FALLING WITHIN SPECIFIED CLASSES LISTED IN THE REGULATIONS ARE AUTOMATICALLY APPROVED AS INCREASES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even where automatic approval applies, applicants still must obtain approval from the stabilization agency. Agency approval may be considered in determining price or rent ceilings. When approval is obtained the employer may use these increases (or increased costs to the Government) as a basis for seeking an increase in price ceilings or for other price/rent relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of approved increases in price/rent ceiling determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: When stabilization-agency approval is obtained the employer may use these increases — or increased costs to the Government — as a basis for seeking an increase in price ceilings or for increased costs to the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stabilization-agency approvals can be factored into price or rent ceiling adjustments; approval status may influence Office of Price Administration decisions. The regulations tie wage/salary approvals to potential price relief actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral / designation of industries for pre-approval
rubrics_metrics.description: THE ADMINISTRATOR WILL NOT DESIGNATE AN INDUSTRY EXCEPT ON THE RECOMMENDATION OF AN INTERESTED GOVERNMENT AGENCY AND WHILE HE IS SATISFIED THAT SPECIFIC STANDARDS PROVIDED IN THE REGULATIONS HAVE BEEN MET.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An industry may be designated for pre-approval only following a recommending government agency and subject to satisfaction of regulatory standards; designation enables use of pre-approval pathways for wage/salary adjustments in that industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of pre-existing lawful increases (pre-August 18, 1945)
rubrics_metrics.description: Wage or salary adjustments lawfully made or approved by the appropriate wage or salary stabilization agency before August 18, 1945 are acknowledged by the regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjustments lawfully made or approved prior to Aug. 18, 1945 qualify under specified transitional or grandfathering provisions; agencies should verify lawfulness and effective dates when considering such increases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increases made under pre-existing wage/salary schedules
rubrics_metrics.description: Made in accordance with the terms and conditions of a wage or salary schedule lawfully in effect before August 18, 1945.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raises that follow an existing lawful schedule in force before the cutoff date are treated as conforming adjustments; documentation of the schedule and its lawful status is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increases under War Labor Board or Salary Stabilization Unit rules for new piece/job rates
rubrics_metrics.description: MADE IN ACCORDANCE WITH REQUIREMENTS OF WAR LABOR BOARD OR SALARY STABILIZATION UNIT REGULATIONS REGARDING THE INSTITUTION OF NEW PIECE RATES OR NEW JOB RATES IN LINE WITH EXISTING PIECE OR JOB RATES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjustments instituted under the War Labor Board or Salary Stabilization Unit procedures for establishing new piece or job rates (consistent with existing rates) are recognized; agencies should check conformity with those prior procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of small corrective increases to remedy substandard living
rubrics_metrics.description: MADE IN ACCORDANCE WITH EXISTING ORDERS OF THE WAR LABOR BOARD REGARDING INCREASES UP TOSS CENTS AN HOUR TO CORRECT SUBSTANDARDS OF LIVING.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre‑existing War Labor Board orders authorizing modest hourly increases to correct substandard living are treated as allowable adjustments under the regulations. (Text is OCR‑imperfect; agencies should consult the authoritative regulatory text for exact cents-per-hour limits.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance to Office of Price Administration on price relief applications
rubrics_metrics.description: STANDARDS ARE PROVIDED TO GUIDE THE OFFICE OF PRICE ADMINISTRATION IN DEALING WITH APPLICATIONS FOR PRICE RELIEF, UNDER THE PROVISION OF EXECUTIVE ORDER 9651 THAT UNAPPROVED WAGE-OR SALARY ADJUSTMENTS SHALL BE TAKEN INTO CONSIDERATION IN DETERMINING PRICE OR RENT CEILINGS AFTER THE EXPIRATION OF A REASONABLE TEST PERIOD — GENERALLY SIX MONTHS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unapproved wage/salary adjustments must nevertheless be considered by OPA in price/rent ceiling determinations after a reasonable test period (usually six months). This ties wage adjustment approvals and their timing to subsequent price relief evaluations.
